name: zzBJ2_avatar_cause

tests.name: the world settled before the first rung was taken
there is a Project Avatar figure on disk to spawn
one Project Avatar stands in the world to measure

detail.note: the 110 ms is the cost of the FIRST one, so a world with none in it has nothing to say.

tests.name: every rung's knob took the value it was given

detail.note: r.DistanceFields refused its value in the previous run -- read back 1.0 after being set to 0 -- and voided that rung. A ladder whose knob refuses measures one rung repeatedly and looks exactly like a term that does not matter.

tests.name: every rung collected enough distinct frames to have a median

detail.note: frames are accepted only when the engine frame number ADVANCES, so a stalled overlay shows up as a thin rung instead of as a suspiciously steady reading.

tests.name: turning shadow casting off on the AVATAR'S OWN components is worth real milliseconds

detail.note: THE ONE RUNG THAT IS A CANDIDATE FIX RATHER THAN A PROBE. It leaves the rest of the world casting shadows normally, so it ships as a property on the avatar rather than as a scalability setting that would degrade the whole scene. Whether the avatars look right without their own shadows is the founder's call, and this only says what it would buy.

tests.name: the avatar this job spawned was taken back out

detail.note: it costs 110 ms of frame while it stands there, so leaving one behind would quietly tax every later measurement in this session and in every other lane's.
